prompt: Competition brings out the best in people.
choices: Competition can push people to excel when the stakes are fair and the goal is mastery, but it brings out their worst when winning matters more than the work itself.
Competition is good and bad.
There are many kinds of competition in the world, such as sports, business and school.
I will discuss competition in this essay.
Competition always brings out the best in everyone.
explanation: The best thesis takes a position and says when it holds and when it does not. The others are vague, merely descriptive, an announcement, or an absolute claim that is easy to attack.

prompt: The study of history is valuable mainly because it helps us avoid repeating past mistakes.
choices: History's chief value lies less in preventing repeated mistakes, which it rarely does, than in teaching us to question how stories about the past are told.
History is a very important subject that everyone should study.
Many mistakes have been made in history.
History helps us avoid mistakes, and it is also interesting.
Some people like history and some do not.
explanation: It engages the specific reason in the prompt, takes a clear stance and proposes an alternative. The others are general or say nothing arguable.

prompt: Governments should spend more on preventing problems than on solving them after they arise.
choices: Prevention deserves a larger share of public spending where risks are predictable and cheap to reduce, as with disease and floods, but not where future problems are too uncertain to target.
Prevention is better than cure.
Governments spend money on many things.
This essay will look at both sides of the issue.
Governments should always spend all their money on prevention.
explanation: It qualifies the position with a clear rule for when prevention makes sense. A proverb, a fact, an announcement and an absolute are weaker.

prompt: Success in any career depends more on persistence than on talent.
choices: In most careers persistence matters more than raw talent, because skill grows with practice, though in a few fields talent sets limits that effort alone cannot pass.
Persistence and talent are both things that people have.
Everyone can succeed if they try hard.
I agree with the statement for many reasons.
Talent is a gift.
explanation: It states a position, gives the core reason and names the exception. The others are vague or unsupported.

prompt: Museums should return objects to the countries they were taken from.
choices: Museums should return objects acquired by force or fraud, but returning every foreign object would empty collections that, shared fairly, educate people across the world.
Museums have many objects from other countries.
Returning objects is a complicated issue with many views.
Museums should keep everything they own.
This essay will discuss museums.
explanation: It draws a clear line between cases and gives a reason for each side. The others describe, hedge or take an extreme view without reasons.

prompt: It is better to know a little about many subjects than a great deal about one.
choices: Breadth matters most early in life, when it helps people choose and connect ideas, but lasting contributions usually require the depth that only focus can give.
Knowledge is power.
There are many subjects in the world to learn about.
Knowing a lot is good.
I disagree completely with this statement.
explanation: It takes a nuanced, arguable position with a reason. The rest are slogans, facts or bare opinions.
